anti_generic_signature_read: Asked cold what it could not have predicted: "that the rank numeral is engraved on the vertical rim of the base rather than on its top face. Every instinct says put the number where the player looking down can read it. Putting it on the side means you read a piece's rank from across the table at eye level... which is exactly where you actually need it during play." And beside it: "the eight balls are sized in true planetary diameter order, which is not an intuitive order (Saturn second, Earth only fifth) and which makes the ladder legible to someone who cannot read the numerals at all -- this is a real design idea, not decoration."
blind_action_read: "You pinch a globe between thumb and forefinger, lift it, and set it down on the next square. The sphere is the handle." And, unprompted, why that matters: "On a normal Jungle set you grip a flat disc or a printed tile; here the thing you grip is a ball, and the balls are graded in size, so you feel the rank in your fingers before you read it. Picking up Jupiter and picking up Mercury are different physical sensations. The rank ladder is encoded in the grip." On capture: "you lift it off the board and drop it into one of the scooped recesses in your tray."
blind_form_read: "Each is two volumes: a low cylindrical puck base and a sphere sitting on a short, narrower collar" -- with the bases measured as a constant (~215 px across all eight) and the ball as the only variable. It catalogued the whole object blind: one board of 63 cells in four types (43 plain, 12 river, 6 trap, 2 den), sixteen pieces, four cones, two trays of eight scoops. On the corona tile it distinguished cut from raised by experiment rather than by assumption: the sunburst "is definitively a cut and not a relief, because corona-cell-top.png -- the same cell seen from directly above -- is a completely featureless orange square. A raised glyph would still show a silhouette from above; this one vanishes."
blind_held_read: Unprompted, before anything was revealed: "a two-player abstract strategy board game set, and the board's topology identifies the game unambiguously: it is Dou Shou Qi / 'Jungle' / Animal Chess, re-skinned as the solar system." It measured the grid from the board's own corners rather than assuming it -- two edge vectors divided by 7 and by 9 giving cell steps of magnitude 46.4 and 44.9, "which agree to within 3%, which is what you get from square cells on a 7 x 9 grid -- and 7 x 9 is exactly the Jungle board." It then found, unaided, the two six-cell rivers, a den at each end and "exactly three marked cells wrapped around each den", and separated what it saw from what it inferred: "the board's geometry I can see; the rules I am inferring from that geometry."
blind_relationship_read: Asked cold, pair by pair, which pairs are two different objects and which are one photographed twice, it answered eight of twelve comparisons as two different objects. On Mercury, from the two same-camera frames: "zero yaw and zero pitch difference between the two shots. Yet the surroundings are swapped... Left and right counts swap while the centred feature stays put. That is a reflection, not a rotation. Highest confidence of anything in this report." On Venus: "In sol the white band enters the left limb low, rises to a peak... In anti the band enters the left limb high and descends... The slope sign reverses." It called Jupiter one object photographed twice -- "I cannot tell these apart and I would not notice if you swapped them" -- which is the evidence the Jupiter decision was taken on.
blind_subjects_read: All eight worlds named cold, each with the cue recorded at the time: Jupiter from "a red oval set in a lighter bay" among horizontal bands; Saturn from "a broad flat annulus -- nothing else in the solar system has a ring that wide"; Uranus from a featureless cyan ball with a ring "standing nearly vertical... A near-perpendicular ring means a planet tipped on its side"; Neptune from a "small dark grey oval low on the disc"; Earth from "Americas / Atlantic / Africa"; Venus from "uniform pale cream-yellow with no dark markings at all, crossed by a single lighter sinuous band"; Mars from a white polar cap and "a distinct downward-pointing wedge... the classic Syrtis Major triangle"; Mercury from "one conspicuous bright ring-shaped feature with a pale floor". Two armies of eight, and no Sun, Moon or Pluto.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round one, unprimed, on the two same-camera frames: "Same camera, same framing, same pose: the bright ring sits at x=458 in both... so there is zero yaw and zero pitch difference between the two shots. Yet the surroundings are swapped... Left and right counts swap while the centred feature stays put. That is a reflection, not a rotation. Highest confidence of anything in this report." In round two it reflected its own recorded round-one boxes about the ball centre and found three marks, three matches, with two of the three top edges landing on the identical y value.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Mercury's two pieces must read as two DIFFERENT objects and as a MIRROR PAIR, where before this revision they were one piece photographed twice.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Tested four independent ways in round two. The decisive one is the grazing frame: "The tile's far silhouette runs as an unbroken straight line from the left vertex through the far vertex to the right vertex. Nothing breaks that skyline anywhere along it. A 4.00 mm horn at a far corner would stand up off that line unmistakably at this angle." All three tiles in the den frame checked corner by corner, all six on the board frame, and all six in each of the three state panels: "Twelve horns, if they were there, are gone, and nothing has been put in their place."

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round one, unprimed and before it knew anything had changed, it separated cut from raised by experiment: "It is definitively a cut and not a relief, because corona-cell-top.png -- the same cell seen from directly above -- is a completely featureless orange square. A raised glyph would still show a silhouette from above; this one vanishes."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The sixteen-rayed star must remain on the trap tile, ENGRAVED into its face rather than standing above it.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round two: "exactly four flames -- cyan at (1070,285) and (1160,310) on the black den, ochre at (410,635) and (505,665) on the cream den. It also named the only candidates for confusion and dismissed them: the belt tiles' crests, "low, wide and numerous where the flames are tall, slender and four."

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Answered in round one, unprimed, by a reader who had never been told what a trap was and did not know anything had been removed. It located all six -- three cyan and three orange -- and gave three reasons: "they are the only cyan cells anywhere on the board"; "each carries an incised radiating sunburst glyph"; "they form a tight ring around the den and nothing else on the board has that arrangement." Round two: "I did not experience the board as having a gap in it."

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round one, unprimed, off the ladder frame: "rank-ladder-sol.png lays all eight out in one row with one camera. The ball diameters fall monotonically left to right: roughly 200 px, 195, 175, 160, 125, 115, 105, 85. Meanwhile every base disc in that row is the same diameter (~215 px). So the base is a constant and the ball is the variable -- the designer deliberately made size the carrier of rank. This is directly visible; you do not need to know anything to see it."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: All eight globes must be comparable at one scale so that rank is something a reader can SEE.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Named blind, and measured rather than guessed: "a two-player abstract strategy board game set, and the board's topology identifies the game unambiguously: it is Dou Shou Qi / 'Jungle' / Animal Chess, re-skinned as the solar system." It derived the 7 x 9 grid from the board's own corners and found the two rivers, the two dens and the three traps around each.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: All eight named cold from surface cues alone, each cue recorded at the time -- Jupiter from its red oval in a lighter bay, Saturn from its broad annulus, Uranus from a near-vertical ring, Neptune from a dark oval under white latitude lines, Earth from "Americas / Atlantic / Africa", Venus from a featureless cream deck with one sinuous band, Mars from a polar cap and the Syrtis wedge, Mercury from "one conspicuous bright ring-shaped feature with a pale floor". critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: "You pinch a globe between thumb and forefinger, lift it, and set it down on the next square. The sphere is the handle." Read blind, with its consequence read blind too: "the balls are graded in size, so you feel the rank in your fingers before you read it."

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Established blind: eight ranked pieces a side on a 7 x 9 board with a den at each end, "two sets of these sphere pieces" carrying the same eight worlds. On the mirroring, round two's summary after measurement: six of the eight pairs read as mirrored pairs -- Saturn, Mars, Earth and Neptune from the lean, Mercury and Venus from the newly mirrored map.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round one, unprimed and before it knew this was a decision: "Left ball: red oval at x=262, ball centre x=259, dx = +3. Right ball: red oval at x=637, ball centre x=630, dx = +7. Same side, same offset, with the same stack of bands above it. I cannot tell these apart and I would not notice if you swapped them." critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round two, measured on the critic's own round-one coordinates: on Mercury, "Three marks on Sol, three marks on Anti, same count; two of the three top edges at identical y (255, 215); the third within 10 px. No latitude moved. Nothing added or removed." On Venus, "band peak at y=318 (Sol) and y=322 (Anti); V-notch at y=348 and y=350. Same segment count, same thickness, same single kink. critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round two, on what is decidable from images: everything catalogued blind in round one -- "the 7 x 9 board, the two six-cell rivers, the two trays with eight scoops each, the dens, the six trap tiles, the rank numerals 1-8 on the base rims, all eight maps -- is present and unchanged in character, and the six unmodified worlds all now resolve as one-map-two-leans, which is consistent with their geometry being untouched." The byte-level statement is separate evidence: measure/revision-part-hashes.md.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Nothing else in the set may have changed: the board, the belt, the trays, the stars and the other six worlds.

largest_risk: The critic's own words, unchanged between rounds and untouched by either correction: "ownership is encoded on the least visible surface of the piece. Rank is carried by the ball -- large, coloured, distinctive, readable across a table. Ownership is carried by a small disc your own hand covers as you reach for it, that hides behind the ball at a low angle, and that vanishes outright when a black base lands on the black den." It hit that ambiguity itself in the endgame panel and could not resolve it. Round two sharpened rather than softened it: "The mirror work is real craft, but it is craft spent on the relationship between the two armies, not on telling them apart... Six of eight worlds now tell you they are a mirrored pair; zero of eight tell you which side they are on." It is out of this revision's scope -- the brief changes three printed parts and forbids touching the discs or the ladder -- and it is recorded rather than answered. Its own fixes, listed: a coloured equator, a tinted hemisphere, a matte-versus-gloss finish, or a taller base that stays visible behind the ball.
resolution:
Three rounds, one independent critic, ZERO geometry repairs: no CAD changed at any point, so the images read blind in round one are the images sealed here. Round one was unprimed on 23 frames balanced 15 whole-object-and-pair against 8 detail, with the eight-globe rank ladder in that set -- the frame the previous attempt at this correction lacked and could not seal without. Rounds two and three are disclosed re-reviews on the same frozen images and are marked as such.

The critic filed twelve defects cold and withdrew six against measurement. Four in round two: the den obstructed by its own flames (0.000000 mm3 shared on all sixteen worlds, and its own re-measurement corroborated it); the base not fitting its cell (it had measured the 33.50 mm well FLOOR and called it a 36.00 mm cell); the two ringed worlds inconsistently transformed; and 'one of the two sets carries a mirrored map' for Earth, Mars and Saturn. That last withdrawal is the one that matters and the critic made it against itself, re-measuring Earth as a ~45-degree rotation with cyclic order preserved and retracting, verbatim, 'a mirrored Earth and a mirrored Mars are not views of anything real.' Two more fell in round three when the assembly's boolean interference check returned clashCount 0 over 220 occurrences over 412 tested pairs, none truncated.

The self-citation check this revision's brief requires was run, in both directions. The record was found accurate; the error it turned up was the critic's own, and it reported it unprompted -- its round-one summary said 'six of twelve comparisons show reflected faces' when its own verdicts counted eight.

What stands, none of it blocking: the 0.40 mm flat-bottomed trap engraving does not read at normal incidence, so from directly above a trap is told by colour and recess (its fix, inside the no-raised-feature rule: a V-groove of the same depth); Jupiter is left uncorrected by decision; and the largest risk, unchanged and out of this revision's scope.
reviewer: One independent native critic. Round 1 unprimed on 23 canonical renders; round 2 a disclosed re-review on the same frozen images. No geometry changed between rounds.
